Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically unless the controller selects another successful step. When asked
to choose among successful steps, reply exactly SELECT <step>. Never select unexecuted code.
Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls: five fresh CLI sessions, three
Blender executions and 1200 seconds. Actual observable model events are logged externally.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position and
returns the attached node. It replaces an existing same-name child. A node already owned by
another parent is cloned; retrieve the returned attachment when editing it afterward.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, *, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, *, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. pivot is keyword-only for turn and resize.
node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies;
pivot and euler are keyword-only.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; opacity is keyword-only.
node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='center', target_anchor=None, offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
For an Asset target, omitted target_anchor uses source_anchor. A target can also be a world
point; then omit target_anchor. For bottom-on-top placement specify both anchors explicitly.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates and returns a copy.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) returns a copy with selected coordinates positioned relative
to the reference centroid or world point; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
For orbit, orient and rotation_offset are keyword-only. Layout functions return assemblies
of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='center',target_anchor='center',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members and immediately settles it.
Endpoints must belong to the scene and cannot be ancestors/descendants of each other.
scene.settle() updates dependencies. Specify bottom/top anchors explicitly for support placement.
realize(scene, clear=True) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Compiler details relevant to editing and shading:
Semantic attachment names label EMPTY parents. Emitted meshes use primitive node names;
use descendant traversal beneath a semantic parent to target its meshes. Materials are cached
by exact RGBA finish and may be shared across unrelated objects. Copy materials for local edits.
Object texture coordinates need an explicit shared reference object for continuous patterns
across separately transformed primitive meshes. Generated coordinates are per-mesh normalized.
Bounds and Boolean support approximations do not establish true contact or collision.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)


Shared reconstruction procedure:
Return a complete first build immediately, with a short planning ledger in code comments.
List every prominent object, including cropped foreground objects, its approximate normalized
image bounds, visible supports, silhouette-defining parts and occlusion order. Record 5-8
reference anchors distributed across foreground, subject and architecture, plus perspective
line directions and a camera hypothesis. These are visual estimates, not calibration.
Keep camera, major dimensions, placements, material palette and lighting parameters together.

Compact means economical representation, not missing surfaces or semantic parts. Establish
all major objects and their distinctive profiles in the first build. Allocate geometry to
visible changes in contour, thickness, curvature and negative space before small ornament.
Do not represent a broad shaped panel solely with a tubular outline; supply its filled body.
Do not substitute an oval for a visibly angular cushion or a constant-radius rail for a broad
shaped apron merely to reduce mesh count. Use short connected SceneAct assemblies to capture
such profiles. Match silhouette and projected proportions before surface microdetail.

Use a named Asset for each independently editable semantic object. Within it, group attached
subassemblies with their trim, inlays, panels and fixtures. Moving a rail should carry its own
attached edging; moving furniture should carry its frame, upholstery and supports. Separate
independent nearby objects into their own Assets even if they share a wall or material.
Use descriptive stable names, not names chosen to affect an evaluator's target ordering.
Before realize, inspect source membership against the object ledger, including nested groups.
A passing edit on a helper assembly does not certify a complete semantic object.
Print a compact inventory of top-level child names and descendant primitive counts, and the
whole-scene count: sum(n.solid is not None for n in scene.traverse()). Count expanded primitives,
not helper calls. Numeric primitive targets are unvalidated planning heuristics, not quality
criteria or hard limits. Remove repeated subpixel detail before simplifying major silhouettes.
Prefer simple assemblies to Boolean operations; use restrained shaders for surface patterns.

Implementation semantics to respect:
- include(name,node) replaces a child with that name. Use unique loop names. Attaching a node
  owned by a different parent clones it; use the returned node for subsequent attachment edits.
- fillet_box requires 0 < radius <= min(size)/2, including thickness. It emits up to 23 meshes.
  sweep_tube with N points emits N spheres and N-1 cylinders. Use rod for straight members;
  use enough distinct control points for visible curves, without dense ornamental sweeps.
- Dimensions, radii and coordinates must be finite; dimensions and radii must be positive.
  Rod endpoints must differ. Avoid empty groups in bounding-box calculations.
- Transform a complete group around an explicit meaningful pivot when preserving support or
  attachment matters. Default pivots are world AABB centers, not necessarily asset origins.
  AABB landmarks and support candidates do not establish true mesh contact or collision.
- realize clears Blender and its world. Create all bpy materials, camera and lights afterward.
  sc = bpy.context.scene
  if sc.world is None:
      sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('Ambient')
  sc.world.use_nodes = True
  Do not retain pre-realize bpy references.
- Geometry must use SceneAct. Do not create meshes or curves through bpy or change the library.

Material assignment and pattern coordinates:
SceneAct emits semantic attachment names on EMPTY markers; meshes retain primitive node names
such as Box, Ball and Rod. Searching mesh names for attachment labels can silently match nothing.
After realize, locate the intended semantic marker and traverse its descendants to find meshes.
For each targeted assignment, count matched meshes and assert the expected set is nonempty.
The compiler shares materials by exact RGBA finish. Copy a material before changing just one
object's appearance; changing a shared material affects all its users. Assign copied materials
only to intended descendants, preserving other objects. A palette match is appropriate only
when every user of that finish should receive the same treatment.
Generated coordinates normalize each primitive separately. Object texture coordinates without
an explicit reference object are also local to each mesh, not continuous world coordinates.
A scaled box can therefore stretch a supposedly small floor pattern over the entire floor.
For continuous patterns across an assembly, use a common existing semantic EMPTY as the explicit
ShaderNodeTexCoord.object and connect its Object output; account for that marker's transform.
Choose pattern spacing in that shared coordinate frame from visible repetition in the image.
Do not create geometry for fabric stitches or tiny floor seams. Keep floor seams restrained,
cloth patterns low contrast, and the large material color regions faithful to the reference.

Revision discipline:
Compare the reference and actual render using the anchor ledger, recording both approximate
positions and residual directions in code comments. Separate three questions:
1. Camera: do architecture and multiple independent objects show a coherent framing or
   perspective residual? Lens changes at fixed pose change framing; camera translation changes
   depth-dependent ratios. Neither alone proves the true camera. Do not fit only the main object
   while ignoring wall edges, foreground crops or background anchors.
2. Geometry: with a plausible camera, which local contours, projected dimensions, supports or
   occlusions remain wrong? Edit the entire relevant semantic group, or its complete subassembly.
   Scaling a helper rail is not a test of whole-object scale. Avoid global scaling for local shape.
3. Appearance: with camera and geometry fixed, compare large brightness/color regions, material
   assignment, texture scale, roughness and light direction. Verify shader targeting and coordinate
   semantics before compensating with color or light intensity. Avoid simultaneous large changes
   to albedo and illumination unless there is a specific explanation.
Choose the largest evidence-supported correction family per revision. Preserve matched anchors
and all ledger objects; document any necessary coupled change. Prefer essential silhouette
corrections to fine decoration. An unrendered rewrite has no demonstrated improvement.

Failures and budgets:
Five fresh CLI sessions, three Blender executions and 1200 seconds are hard limits. The external
logger counts actual model events; one session need not equal one observable turn. Work only
through the supplied controller. Do not use tools, other models, filesystem exploration or network.
Never render extra views, save files or modify the fixed renderer's engine, resolution, sampling
or resource settings. Noise alone is not a reason to change renderer settings.
On failure, use the actual exception/logs to repair the cause and audit the semantics above.
Missing output is failure; do not describe an unseen render. A timeout without stage logs does
not identify the stalled stage. Simplifying repeated detail is a conservative recovery option,
not proof that geometry caused the timeout. Preserve complete objects and supports when reducing
cost. DONE is allowed only after inspecting a successful render. SELECT <step> may choose only
one of the supplied successful rendered steps. In selection-only mode, generate no new code.

from sceneact import *

# Appearance residual: parquet is too bright/orange; fabric pattern too faint.

# label .68,.53-.71,.59; paneled wall .04,0-1,.55;
# curtain/window 0,0-.08,.78; parquet lower half;
# cropped cane chair 0,.80-.19,1; right wall return .85,0-1,.56.
# Occlusion: wall/window -> chaise frame -> mattress/pillow/card -> foreground chair.
# Supports: chaise's four cabriole feet and chair legs meet parquet at z=0.
# Perspective hypothesis: elevated front view, almost normal to wall,
# with chaise yaw producing its slight downward-right mattress edge.

    'camera': (-.72,-5.65,3.68),

scene=Scene('French chaise room')

def add(p,n,v):

def tube(p,n,pts,r,c):
    return add(p,n,sweep_tube(points=pts,radius=r,color=c))

def ellipsoid(size,center,color):

for z,d,h in [(.10,.10,.18),(.235,.065,.045),(.31,.045,.035),

add(chaise,'seat_foundation',fillet_box((2.40,1.045,.12),radius=.055,

for y in [-.518,.518]:
    tube(chaise,f'seat_welting_{y}',
        [(-1.03,y,.70),(-.75,y,.683),(.20,y,.68),(1.12,y,.68),(1.27,y,.72)],
        .012,(.64,.57,.44))

for y in [-.535,.535]:
    apron=Part(f'apron_{y}')
    xs=[-1.01,-.80,-.47,-.13,.20,.53,.86,1.12,1.25]
    lower=[.49,.47,.485,.46,.43,.46,.48,.46,.48]
    for i in range(len(xs)-1):
        mid=(xs[i]+xs[i+1])/2
        bottom=(lower[i]+lower[i+1])/2
        add(apron,f'filled_rail_{i}',box(
            (xs[i+1]-xs[i],.055,.61-bottom),
            center=(mid,y,(.61+bottom)/2),color=P['wood']))
    front=y+(-.033 if y<0 else .033)
    tube(apron,'upper_gilt_line',[(x,front,.603) for x in xs],.009,P['edge'])
    tube(apron,'lower_gilt_line',[(x,front,z) for x,z in zip(xs,lower)],.012,P['edge'])
    add(chaise,f'apron_{y}',apron)

    for iy,y in enumerate([-.45,.45]):
        out=-1 if x<0 else 1
        pts=[(x,y,.56),(x+out*.065,y,.44),(x+out*.025,y,.30),
             (x-out*.035,y,.13),(x-out*.012,y,.055)]
        tube(chaise,f'cabriole_{ix}_{iy}',pts,.036,P['wood'])

             [(a,b-.025,c) for a,b,c in pts],.007,P['edge'])
        add(chaise,f'foot_{ix}_{iy}',ellipsoid((.050,.041,.027),
            (pts[-1][0],y,.045),P['wood']))

    y=-.50+(k+.5)/16

    crest=1.49+.10*math.sin(s*math.pi)
    x=-1.065-.13*math.sin(s*math.pi)
    panel=box((.14,1/16,crest-.75),
        center=(x,y,(crest+.75)/2),color=P['cloth'])
    panel.turn('y',-12,pivot=(x,y,.75))
    add(back,f'filled_back_{k}',panel)
top=[(-1.105-.13*math.sin(k/12*math.pi),-.5+k/12,
      1.49+.10*math.sin(k/12*math.pi)) for k in range(13)]
tube(back,'crest_wood',top,.037,P['wood'])
tube(back,'crest_highlight',[(x+.006,y-.018,z+.017) for x,y,z in top],
     .010,P['edge'])
add(chaise,'head_back',back)

for side in [-1,1]:
    wing=Part(f'wing_{side}')
    xs=[-1.07,-.95,-.82,-.68,-.53,-.43]
    tops=[1.47,1.31,1.20,1.15,1.13,1.16]
    bottoms=[.70,.68,.65,.64,.65,.69]

    for k in range(len(xs)-1):
        for q in range(3):
            t0=q/3
            t1=(q+1)/3
            x0=xs[k]+(xs[k+1]-xs[k])*t0

            add(wing,f'filled_side_{k}_{q}',box((x1-x0,.078,ztop-bot),

    tube(wing,'arm_rail',[(x,side*.50,z) for x,z in zip(xs,tops)],.033,P['wood'])
    tube(wing,'arm_gilt',[(x,side*.525,z+.011) for x,z in zip(xs,tops)],.009,P['edge'])
    tube(wing,'lower_frame',[(x,side*.51,z) for x,z in zip(xs,bottoms)],.027,P['wood'])
    tube(wing,'front_upright',

         (-.43,side*.51,.69)],.026,P['wood'])

card=Asset('green_museum_label')

for k in range(3):
    add(card,f'printed_line_{k}',box((.039,.003,.001),
        center=(.84,.18-k*.018,.885),color=(.73,.77,.65)))

# Apply the same meaningful floor-origin rotation to the three independent objects.
for name,node in [('chaise_longue',chaise),('loose_pillow',pillow),
                  ('green_museum_label',card)]:
    node.turn('z',P['yaw'],pivot=(0,0,0))

cx,cy=-1.57,-1.55
add(chair,'seat_rim',fillet_box((.65,.64,.065),radius=.031,
    center=(cx,cy,.49),color=P['wood']))

    color=(.46,.31,.17)))

    for iy,y in enumerate([cy-.24,cy+.24]):
        add(chair,f'leg_{ix}_{iy}',rod(.029,
            start=(x,y,.02),end=(x,y,.49),color=P['wood']))
scene.include('cropped_foreground_cane_chair',chair)

# Audit complete semantic memberships, including all attached subassemblies.
for name,node in scene.members.items():
    print(name,sum(n.solid is not None for n in node.traverse()))
print('whole_scene',sum(n.solid is not None for n in scene.traverse()))
realize(scene)

def descendants(name):
    marker=bpy.data.objects.get(name)
    if marker is None:
        found=[o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type=='EMPTY' and o.name.startswith(name)]
        assert found,name
        marker=found[0]
    meshes=[o for o in marker.children_recursive if o.type=='MESH']
    assert meshes,name
    return marker,meshes

def fabric_material(name,base,striped=False):
    m=bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes=True
    n=m.node_tree.nodes
    l=m.node_tree.links
    bs=n.get('Principled BSDF')
    bs.inputs['Roughness'].default_value=.88
